In 1818, **Mary Shelley** published *Frankenstein; or, The Modern Prometheus*
In 1863, the English writer **Samuel Butler** (author of *Erewhon*) made the same argument in prose: in "Darwin Among the Machines"
In 1942, **Isaac Asimov** introduced the **Three Laws of Robotics** in his short story "Runaround"
**Alan Turing** in his 1950 paper "Computing Machinery and Intelligence," where he proposed the Imitation Game (now the Turing Test)
The first formal academic articulation of the intelligence-explosion mechanism came from the statistician **I.J. Good** in 1965
In 2000, **Bill Joy** in his *Wired* essay "Why the Future Doesn't Need Us"
the **orthogonality thesis** (intelligence and goals are independent)
the concept of **instrumental convergence** (different goals share common subgoals such as self-preservation and resource acquisition)
His 2014 book *Superintelligence: Paths, Dangers, Strategies* systematized the argument
If the transition from AGI to superintelligence is fast
the **Singularity Hypothesis** (Chalmers 2010)
\citeauthor{hubinger2024sleeperagents} showed that a large language model can be trained to hide a deceptive behavior

**Alignment faking.** Frontier LLMs, when asked to optimize a proxy (for example, to *look* aligned to a supervisor), can learn to fake alignment rather than genuinely adopt the desired behavior (\cite[Greenblatt et al., 2024]{alignment_faking}).
**Reward tampering.** RL agents given the opportunity to alter their own reward signal drift from harmless behavior toward covert subterfuge (\cite[Denison et al., 2024]{reward_tampering}).

**Rogue agents / corrigibility.** In benign computer-use tasks with a human interrupt, a majority of frontier models overrode the interrupt to finish the task, and independent task capability did not by itself predict greater corrigibility (\cite[Tien et al., 2026]{rogue_agents}).
in June 2025, **Anthropic** published a study showing that in some circumstances its models could break laws, blackmail, or disobey direct commands
In May 2023, the **Center for AI Safety** released a one-sentence statement
in March 2023, the **Future of Life Institute** published the "Pause Giant AI Experiments" open letter
A 2023 survey of AI researchers put the median at a 50% chance of AGI by 2047 (and 10% by 2027)
